1Executive summary

The verdict: the index is masking the damage. SPY closed Friday 2.8% off its all-time high, dead on its rising daily EMA50 (738.9), inside a three-week 735–755 range — while beneath it the complex that led the whole 2025–26 advance is in open correction: QQQ −8.6% from high with lower-highs/lower-lows on the daily, SMH −16.5% after a synchronized June 30 blow-off top across semis (AMD 584.73, MRVL 329.88, INTC 142.35), software (IGV) −25% in its own structural bear, and three former leaders — ORCL, CRWV, TSLA — in outright distribution. Sentiment is fearful (CNN Fear & Greed 38.8), single-name ATRs are the widest in months, and this week stacks a Wednesday FOMC against MSFT + META (Wed AMC) and AAPL + AMZN (Thu AMC) earnings with GDP and Core PCE Thursday morning. This is an event-driven, level-to-level tape — a day-trader's market, not a fresh-swing-entry market.

5Day-trading playbook

Key levels and market structure are exactly the right toolkit for this tape — this section turns the level maps in Section 6 into an intraday process. The environment: daily ATRs of 5–10% across half the list, fear-regime sentiment, and binary catalysts mid-week. That combination pays level-to-level trading and punishes both chasing and averaging-down.

Session-by-session frame

SessionFrame
MonGap-up ≈+1% into pre-FOMC drift. The gap opens SPY above the 744–745 shelf (daily EMA10/21): hold above 745 = long bias to 750, then 752.4; a first-hour failure back under 744 sets up gap-fill shorts toward 741.5/739.5. Expect fade-prone, two-sided tape; oversold names (TSLA, SPCX, CRWV) carry Friday-afternoon bounce momentum on the 15m.
TueRange day risk into Wednesday. KLAC/STX AMC = semi read-through for Wednesday's SMH open. Trade smaller; take profits at range edges.
WedNo-trade window ≈13:30–14:45 ET around FOMC statement + presser start. The 14:30–16:00 post-presser move is often the week's first real trend leg — trade it with the index level map (SPY 735/739/745/750/755). MSFT, META, HOOD report AMC: day-trade positions in these should be flat by the close.
ThuGDP + Core PCE 08:30 sets the open; earnings reactions in MSFT/META/HOOD dominate the first hour — trade the reaction structure (opening range, first pullback), never the pre-market gap itself. AAPL + AMZN AMC.
FriAAPL/AMZN gap day + month-end. Post-earnings trend days are this tape's best R:R — wait for the 15–30 min opening range, trade the break with VWAP on your side.

Setups this week, in priority order

SetupHow to trade it
1 · Post-event opening-range break (Wed PM, Thu, Fri)After FOMC / earnings gaps: mark the first 15–30 min high/low; trade the break in the direction of the gap if 15m RVOL > 2.5 and price is on the right side of VWAP. Target the next mapped daily level; stop the other side of the range. This is the A+ trade of the week.
2 · 200-day reclaim/failure (GOOGL 319.4 · HOOD 92.7 · AMZN 235.8)Reclaim + hold above on a 15m closing basis = long to the next supply shelf (GOOGL 324→330; HOOD 96.6→100; AMZN 238→242). Rejection = short the retest with the level as your stop. Do not hold through the name's own earnings.
3 · Capitulation-bounce continuation (TSLA > 318.5 · SPCX > 117 · CRWV > 74.7)These printed reversal candles Friday PM at major supports (TSLA at its weekly EMA200 307). Above the trigger, ride toward the first 1H supply (TSLA 323.4→330.9; SPCX 119.7→121.6; CRWV 79.5). No trigger, no trade — catching these early is how accounts die.
4 · Range fade (SPY 735–755 · AMD 460–585 · PLTR 120.7–138.9)Pre-FOMC only (Mon/Tue): fade tests of the range edge with tight stops when RVOL is low — a high-RVOL test is a break, not a fade.
5 · Lower-high fade in distribution (ORCL < 120 · MRVL < 215 · INTC < 96.4 · CRWV < 85)Short rallies into the declining 1H EMA21/50 with the prior lower-high as stop. Cover into prior lows — don't press new lows in names down 40–60% (bounce risk is violent; ORCL/CRWV 15m RSI already < 26 Friday).

Standing rules for this regime

1) Size by ATR — risk a fixed account fraction per ATR-based stop, never fixed shares. 2) RVOL is the confirmation filter — structure breaks without 15m RVOL > 2.5 revert more often than they run. 3) VWAP is the intraday bias line — longs above, shorts below, no exceptions in extreme-ATR names. 4) Flat into binaries — no day-trade inventory through FOMC 14:00 or through an AMC print in the reporting name. 5) The morning re-anchor — these levels are the map; the daily premarket scan (gap, slot-RVOL, PMH/PML) re-anchors entries each session. 6) Oversold ≠ long — in LH/LL structure, oversold RSI is fuel for the next leg down until a higher-low prints on the 1H or daily.

7Methodology & data notes

Pipeline: TradingView Desktop (CDP) → dedicated "B List Research" layout → up to 500 bars per timeframe per symbol (W / D / 240 / 60 / 15, regular sessions) → indicators computed locally: EMA 10/21/50/200, RSI-14 (Wilder), MACD 12/26/9, ATR-14 (Wilder), 20-bar relative volume, fractal (2-2) swing pivots, 252-day high/low distances, relative strength vs SPY as return differentials. Trend matrix rubric per cell: close vs EMA21 & EMA50, EMA21/50 stack, RSI zone (≥55 / ≤42), MACD histogram sign — score ≥+3 Up, ≤−3 Down, else Chop.

Data caveats: prices as of Friday Jul 24 2026 regular-session close; the weekly bar is complete, intraday last bars are final session bars. Monday pre-market indication (SPY ≈ +1.0%) noted where stated, captured ~06:45 ET Jul 27. SPCX, CRWV and SKHY have short listing histories — long-lookback fields are unavailable and marked "—". Earnings dates/times from the Nasdaq calendar (Jul 27 fetch); FOMC from the Federal Reserve schedule; econ consensus from the public calendar — verify all event times before trading. 52-week figures use the trailing 252 daily bars loaded.
